description: Golden feed-reading cases, asserted by core/test/feed.test.js and reproduced by the iOS client's UpdateFeed.swift (mobile/ClawTests/UpdateFeedParityTests.swift). Each case is a fetched releases document and the build reading it: `newer` is the version newerVersion(document, current) must return, or null when the banner must stay absent. `throws` marks the one case a current version this build cannot parse must throw on rather than silently suppress. The document is the shape a client hands the reader after parsing releases.atom: `entries`, newest-first, each carrying the `id` (which ends in the release tag) and `title` of one Atom <entry>. THE SIGNAL THAT DECIDES "NEWER" IS THE FEED'S OWN ORDERING, never a ranking of the build and commit tail: that tail's basis has changed, so ranking it inverted and the check silently stopped offering builds (see compareRelease in core/version.js). The comparison is the release only, and an entry's position in this document is what says which build is the latest. The case named "an older release is not newer" used to carry an older BUILD of the same release, which the old rule could rank and the new one cannot: it now carries a genuinely older RELEASE, which is the one thing the comparison may still refuse. This is the contract that keeps the two clients reading one feed the same way.

cases.name: a newer dev build is announced
the same build is not newer, so nothing is announced
an older release is not newer
an older stable release is not newer
the reported bug: an installed OLD-SCHEME tail that looks HIGHER than the feed's is still offered the newest build
the feed's tails running BACKWARDS still announce the newest by feed order
a genuinely older release is not offered, so the check has not simply become always-on
the build we are running, first on the channel, is still not newer
a higher dev count is newer whatever the sha
the newest matching entry wins over older ones below it
a dev build skips a newer stable release and reads its own channel
a stable build skips dev releases and reads the newest stable
a dev build is not offered a stable release even when it is the only entry
a document with no entries announces nothing
an entry whose tag does not parse is skipped, not thrown on
an entry tag without a v prefix is still read
a current version this build cannot parse is a surfaced fault

releaseNotes.name: a version names that release's own notes
a stable version names its release too
with no version to name, the channel's list of releases
an empty or blank version is the same as none
